objective: Preserve rollback recoverability and auth smoke coverage for the retired LifeUp bridge while preventing unrelated current-System owner/routing documentation changes from rebuilding the retired container. Broad static contract checks remain active; legacy Docker build/smoke runs only when the legacy bridge implementation or its workflow changes.

roles_before.artifact: lifeup-system-ci static-contract validates that ChatGPT/Neon owns the current System and LifeUp remains retired/rollback-only across owner/routing/controller artifacts.
lifeup-system-ci docker-build builds the retired Northflank LifeUp image and smoke-tests health/auth boundaries.
system/lifeup/northflank remains physically recoverable rollback code and is not part of the target runtime.
projects/lifeup-system.md changes trigger current-System contract validation and continuity without changing legacy bridge code.
Git history and the exact candidate base preserve the previous always-build CI behavior.

role_dispositions.destination: Keep the broad workflow trigger and static-contract job for owner/routing/controller/current-System changes.
Keep the same Docker build and health/auth smoke steps, gated by a deterministic changed-path decision that is true for legacy bridge/workflow changes.
Do not modify or remove the retired northflank rollback implementation.
Owner-only changes still trigger static contract/continuity validation but no longer require an unrelated retired-container rebuild.
Base SHA f5edeeeaa8c36562ab0817f27dc8a1594c6bcc7a and Git history preserve the prior workflow for rollback/audit.

capability_probes.assertion: Any change under system/lifeup/northflank still executes the legacy Docker build and health/auth smoke test.
A projects/lifeup-system.md-only change still runs the static current-System contract but does not build the retired LifeUp image.
Changing lifeup-system-ci.yml itself forces the legacy Docker build/smoke so CI-routing edits cannot bypass their own verification.
Changes to current controller/routing/owner artifacts continue to run the static retirement/current-System contract.
The exact base SHA restores the previous always-build-on-broad-trigger behavior with no data migration.

tests.expected: Owner-only paths return false; northflank implementation and workflow paths return true; mixed changes fail closed to true.
Current System routing remains ChatGPT/Neon, legacy artifacts remain recoverable/secret-safe, and the workflow retains deterministic legacy Docker gating.

tests.command: lifeup-system-ci docker-build on this workflow-changing candidate
tests.expected: Because the workflow itself changed, candidate CI executes and passes the unchanged legacy image build plus health/auth smoke test.
Architecture manifest and ordinary continuity checks pass.

verification.diff_scope: Base f5edeeeaa8c36562ab0817f27dc8a1594c6bcc7a to candidate 21c78c74c3a614f942239d7881737e562dbb19e7 changes exactly four declared paths: lifeup-system-ci workflow, this manifest, deterministic CI-scope helper and the existing LifeUp contract guard. The retired northflank bridge implementation itself is unchanged.

candidate_ci.detail: scope self-test and static contract passed; workflow-change detection forced the legacy Docker build plus health/auth smoke and both passed

verification.adversarial_finding: The first candidate exposed a path-normalization bug: lstrip('./') removed the leading dot from .github and could skip Docker verification for a workflow change. The candidate was not promoted. Normalization was corrected to remove only an exact './' prefix, a regression case was added for both .github and ./.github forms, and the subsequent candidate proved the workflow-change path forces Docker build/smoke.
verification.unintended_capability_loss: none found in base-to-head review or candidate CI; rollback image remains buildable and auth-smoke verified
